title: How was the weekend?
goal: Tell someone what you did last weekend, last summer or two days ago — choosing between the past and the perfect, and pinning every event to the right moment in time.
bekal: past vs perfect: *Var de bra?* vs *Har du hört dem?*
past time words: *i fredags, i somras, förra veckan, för två dagar sedan*
reacting to someone's news: *Vad kul! Vad synd! Vad mysigt!*
wave: Go back to Swedish 101, Unit 15 and Unit 16: read both dialogues aloud, then retell Oskar's weekend at the cottage in Dalarna in five sentences without looking — every verb in the past.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Måndag morgon på campus
dialogs.intro: A new school year has begun — Dian's second in Stockholm. On Monday morning she runs into Oskar outside the lecture hall. Both of them have a weekend to report.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.id: Hi Dian! How was the weekend?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jättebra, tack! I fredags var jag på konsert med Elin och hennes bror Jonas.
lines.id: Great, thanks! Last Friday I went to a concert with Elin and her brother Jonas.
lines.literal: giant-good, thanks! in Friday's was I at concert with Elin and her brother Jonas.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Jonas? Han som spelar i ett band?
lines.id: Jonas? The one who plays in a band?
lines.literal: Jonas? he who plays in a band?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ja, precis. Bandet hade en spelning på en liten klubb på Söder. Har du hört dem någon gång?
lines.id: Yes, exactly. The band had a gig at a little club on Söder. Have you ever heard them?
lines.literal: yes, exactly. band-the had a gig at a little club on South. have you heard them some time?

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Nej, aldrig. Men jag har läst om dem. Var de bra?
lines.id: No, never. But I've read about them. Were they good?
lines.literal: no, never. but I have read about them. were they good?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Riktigt bra! Vi kom inte hem förrän klockan två på natten.
lines.id: Really good! We didn't get home until two in the morning.
lines.literal: really good! we came not home before clock-the two on night-the.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Och i lördags? Sov du länge?
lines.id: And on Saturday? Did you sleep in?
lines.literal: and in Saturday's? slept you long?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Till tolv! Sedan vilade jag hela dagen, och på kvällen lagade jag middag åt Ahmad. Och du?
lines.id: Till twelve! Then I rested all day, and in the evening I made dinner for Ahmad. And you?
lines.literal: till twelve! then rested I whole day-the, and on evening-the cooked I dinner for Ahmad. and you?

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Jag åkte hem till Göteborg i torsdags. Mamma fyllde femtio.
lines.id: I went home to Göteborg on Thursday. My mom turned fifty.
lines.literal: I went home to Göteborg in Thursday's. mom filled fifty.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Grattis till henne! Hade ni kalas?
lines.id: Congratulations to her! Did you have a party?
lines.literal: congrats to her! had you party?

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Ja, i söndags. Hela släkten kom. Jag har inte ätit så mycket sedan i julas.
lines.id: Yes, on Sunday. The whole family came. I haven't eaten that much since last Christmas.
lines.literal: yes, in Sunday's. whole relatives-the came. I have not eaten so much since in Christmas's.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Vad mysigt! Själv har jag inte varit i Göteborg sedan i somras.
lines.id: How lovely! I haven't been to Göteborg myself since last summer.
lines.literal: how cozy! self have I not been in Göteborg since in summer's.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Mamma frågade om dig förresten. Hon undrar när du kommer tillbaka.
lines.id: Mom asked about you, by the way. She's wondering when you're coming back.
lines.literal: mom asked about you by-the-way. she wonders when you come back.

lines.text: Gärna snart! Kanske om två veckor?
lines.id: Soon, I'd love to! Maybe in two weeks?
lines.literal: gladly soon! maybe in two weeks?

lines.text: Perfekt. Jag ringer henne ikväll och säger det.
lines.id: Perfect. I'll call her tonight and tell her.
lines.literal: perfect. I call her tonight and say it.

notes: **I fredags** means "last Friday": take *i*, add an **-s** to the day, and you are in the past — *i måndags, i tisdags, i lördags, i söndags*. In speech the *g* of *fredag* disappears, so it sounds like **i FREH-dahs**. Compare **på fredag** (this coming Friday) and **på fredagar** (on Fridays, every week). Three small words, three different Fridays.

**I somras, i julas** — the same *i … -s* trick works for seasons and holidays: *i vintras* (last winter), *i våras* (last spring), *i höstas* (last fall), *i påskas* (last Easter). Drop the *-s* and you point forward instead: *i sommar* (this summer), *i jul* (this Christmas).

**Har du hört dem någon gång?** but **Var de bra?** — Oskar first asks about experience with no time attached, so he uses the perfect. As soon as one particular evening is in play, the past takes over. English works the same way ("Have you ever heard them?" / "Were they good?"), so trust your instinct here.

**Vi kom inte hem förrän klockan två** — *inte … förrän* means "not until". Don't translate *förrän* as "before" in this pattern. Swedes also say it the short way: *Vi kom hem **först** klockan två* — here *först* means "not until, only then".

**Mamma fyllde femtio** — literally "Mom filled fifty". *Att fylla år* is how Swedes have a birthday: *När fyller du år?* (When is your birthday?), *Hon fyller trettio i maj.* A birthday party is **ett kalas** (**kah-LAHS**) — the word is used for children's parties and family celebrations alike.

**Vad mysigt!** — after *vad* ("how!"), an adjective takes the *-t* form: *Vad mysigt! Vad roligt! Vad trevligt!* A few adjectives never change, so *Vad kul!* and *Vad synd!* stay as they are. *Mysig* (**MÜ-see**) is the Swedish cousin of Danish *hygge*: candles, blankets, good company. **Söder** is what Stockholmers call the island of Södermalm.

grammars.title: Past or perfect?
body: Swedish chooses between the two tenses much as English does. The question to ask is always the same: **is a finished moment named or clearly understood?** If yes, use the past. If no — or if the time stretches up to now — use the perfect (*har* + supine).

head: Situation
Tense
Example
rows: a finished moment: *igår, i fredags, 2019, när jag var liten*
an event both speakers already have in mind
experience, no time given: *någon gång, aldrig, ofta*
from a point in the past up to now: *sedan, i två år*
Jag **har** inte **ätit** så mycket sedan i julas.
a period that isn't over yet: *i dag, i år, den här veckan*
Jag **har** jobbat mycket den här veckan.

after: *Jag har ätit igår* is as wrong in Swedish as "I have eaten yesterday" is in English. Once a finished time is on the table, the perfect is out.
Swedish has no "-ing" forms, so English "I've been living here for a year" simply becomes *Jag har bott här i ett år.* One perfect does the job of both "have lived" and "have been living".

grammars.title: Twelve strong verbs for every story
body: You met most of these in Swedish 101. They are the verbs that carry almost every weekend story, and all of them are irregular — just like their English cousins. Say each row aloud three times: infinitive, past, supine.
after: **Sa** is the normal form of *sade* today, in speech and in most writing. **Sagt** is pronounced **sahkt**, and **gjorde, gjort** begin with a *y* sound: **YOO-deh, yoot**.
Regular verbs need no list: group 1 ends in *-ade / -at* (*vilade, vilat*), group 2 in *-de / -t* or *-te / -t* (*ringde, ringt; åkte, åkt*), group 3 in *-dde / -tt* (*bodde, bott*).

Future
English (past / future)

blocks.text: Look closely at two pairs. **Förra veckan** takes the definite ending (*veckan*), but **nästa vecka** does not — *nästa* never wants a definite noun after it. And **i helgen** is the same in both columns: only the verb tells you whether the weekend is behind you (*Vad gjorde du i helgen?*) or ahead of you (*Vad ska du göra i helgen?*).
**För … sedan** ("… ago") and **om …** ("in …") are mirror images. In speech *sedan* shrinks to **sen**: *för två dagar sen*. **I fjol** (**i FYOOL**) is a common everyday word for "last year".

blocks.title: Reacting to someone's weekend
items: **Vad kul!** — How fun! · **Vad mysigt!** — How lovely/cozy!
**Vad synd!** — What a shame! · **Oj, vad jobbigt!** — Oh, that sounds tough!
**Låter bra!** — Sounds good! · **Grattis!** — Congratulations!
A Swedish conversation partner expects a small reaction like these after every piece of news. Silence can sound like disinterest.

blocks.text: A good story in Swedish moves forward with time words — and every time word you put first pushes the verb into second place and the subject behind it. *I fredags **var** jag på konsert. På kvällen **lagade** jag middag.* The verb-second rule from Swedish 101 doesn't take a break just because the verbs are in the past.

items: **först** — first · **sedan** (*sen*) — then, after that
**på morgonen / på eftermiddagen / på kvällen** — in the morning / afternoon / evening
**dagen efter** — the day after · **efter det** — after that
**till slut** — in the end, finally

blocks.title: Model story
items: *I fredags gick jag ut med Elin. Först åt vi pizza, sedan gick vi på en spelning. Vi kom inte hem förrän klockan två. Dagen efter sov jag länge, och på kvällen vilade jag bara. Det var en riktigt mysig helg.*
Now write your own: five sentences, five different time words, every verb in the past.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Swedish 101, Unit 16
items: Ask five "have you ever" questions with *någon gång*: *Har du någon gång ätit surströmming? Har du varit i Norrland?*
Answer each one twice: first with the perfect (*Ja, det har jag*), then add a past detail with a time word (*Jag åt det i somras*).

answers: åkte — ätit — var — sett — fyllde — bott
Jag åkte till Göteborg i lördags. — Vi badade i somras. — Hon hade kalas förra veckan. — De kom hem för två dagar sedan. — Jag träffade Elin i söndags.
I fredags var jag på konsert. — Vi kom inte hem förrän klockan två. — Jag har inte varit där sedan i somras. — Min mamma frågade om dig förra veckan. — Har du hört bandet någon gång?

Hur var helgen? — I fredags var jag på konsert med Elin. — Jag har inte sett honom sedan i somras. — Vi kom inte hem förrän klockan två. — Min mamma fyllde femtio förra veckan. — Har du någon gång hört dem?
